messages.content: I need all pending and active mandates of users parath and bhanu

function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.reasoning:
We need to call user_mandates twice: once for parath, once for bhanu. For each, we want status pending and active. But the function signature only allows one status at a time. We can call twice per user: one with status "active", one with status "pending". Or we could call with default (active) and then also call with pending. The user wants all pending and active mandates of users parath and bhanu. So we need to fetch both statuses for each user.

Thus we need to call user_mandates twice for each user. That is four calls. But maybe we can combine? The function only accepts one status. So we need separate calls.

We should output the results. Let's do calls:

1. user_mandates({"name":"parath","status":"active"})
2. user_mandates({"name":"parath","status":"pending"})
3. user_mandates({"name":"bhanu","status":"active"})
4. user_mandates({"name":"bhanu","status":"pending"})

We need to output the results. We'll call them sequentially. Use the function calls.
